text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a weird drop in NDCG on the new reranker after the int8 bring-up on staging. Holdout NDCG@10 went from 0.462 -> 0.421 on sampled-prod-holdout :grimacing:.

matt: Which holdout / which eval harness? numbers + seed pls.

sasha: Quick numbers: NDCG@10 0.462 -> 0.421, MRR@10 0.318 -> 0.305. Holdout is holdout_v11 (sampled from recent traffic). Int8 used PTQ with kvpack=true. I ran a quick harness — artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/rerank/1753219999-int8-priming (link).

anya: @matt can you confirm what went live and when?

deploy-bot: release reranker-v2-int8 rolled to staging at 1753219950 by matt. config: model=ranker-v2, quant=int8-ptq, kvpack=true, priming=on. rollout pct=5%.

eva: priming=on? That's the short-template priming we use for short queries. Could priming interact badly with int8? We previously saw shortquery MRR dips when priming+kvpack used together.

matt: I enabled priming to match prod sampling for the test. Good call — we should ablate. I'll run three evals: (A) priming on int8, (B) priming off int8, (C) fp16 baseline. Will post results.

sasha: Reproducer command for local/harness runs:
```bash
python -m eval.rerank --holdout holdout_v11 --model ranker-v2 --quant int8-ptq --kvpack True --priming True --seed 42
```
Outputs uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/rerank/1753219999-int8-priming/ (logs + topk diffs).

anya: Another thing — check candidate tiebreaking. I noticed tiebreak logic differs between fp16 (stable float sort) and int8 (quant rounding produced equal scores then stable random tie). That can flip topk and change NDCG.

eva: Also housekeeping: holdout_v11 was resampled last week; v10 had fewer short queries. If priming affects short queries more, the resample could amplify the observed change.

matt: Quick run results (smoke): priming on int8 -> NDCG@10 0.421; priming off int8 -> NDCG@10 0.457; fp16 priming on -> NDCG@10 0.463. MRR shows same direction. So priming seems to amplify int8 loss. :eyes: 

sasha: Tokenizer parity check passed. My hypothesis: kvpack packing + priming prefix increases activation scale variance, PTQ clipping/scale chosen for overall distribution might be suboptimal for primed prefixes -> numerical instability.

anya: Proposed plan: 1) run pairwise query-level diff to find flips and slices (short vs long queries), 2) run ablation disabling kvpack on int8, 3) sweep PTQ clip/scale on primed-prefix distribution, 4) check tiebreaking deterministic fix. Aim to finish quick triage before we widen rollout. I'll take 1+2.

eva: Please open an internal issue: tag reranker-v2-int8-priming, attach smoke artifacts, add a request for debug traces that save top10 logits + tokenized prefix for flipped queries.

matt: Pausing further rollout until ablation results land. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
